title: Specify concrete technology stack in architecture records
goal: Ensure architecture planning produces a concrete, reviewable technology stack instead of only describing generic technology categories or offering unselected options.
in_scope: Update the architecture-planning skill to require a dedicated Technology Stack section in ARCHITECTURE.md or the repository's existing architecture document.

For each relevant layer, name the selected or recommended technology concretely, such as language/runtime, application framework, data store, API/integration approach, authentication approach, and deployment platform.
Record each choice's role, rationale, and decision status as Proposed, Confirmed, Open, or Not applicable.
Provide one coherent stack recommendation for the project and distinguish it from alternatives; alternatives alone do not count as a stack decision.

Prioritize languages and frameworks that support clear AI-assisted error feedback through static typing, static analysis, compiler or linter diagnostics, and automated checks; for example, consider TypeScript before JavaScript when both fit the project.
Explain when team familiarity, project constraints, or other requirements justify choosing a stack with weaker static feedback, rather than treating the example as an absolute rule.
When a required stack decision is unresolved, record a concrete provisional recommendation and the question or condition needed to confirm it.
Preserve the skill's requirement to verify current, changeable technology details in authoritative sources and to avoid implementing code or runtime configuration.
out_of_scope: Mandating a fixed stack across projects.
Installing or configuring the selected technologies.
acceptance_criteria: The architecture skill requires a dedicated Technology Stack section/table in the architecture record.
Each relevant stack layer names a concrete technology or a clearly labeled provisional recommendation, rather than only a generic category.
Each choice records its role, rationale, and status; irrelevant layers can be marked Not applicable.
The recommendation explicitly considers how easily AI-assisted review can detect and explain errors, including typing, static analysis, diagnostics, and automated checks.
The skill generally prefers TypeScript over JavaScript when both satisfy project needs, and documents a reason when another choice is better suited.
The architecture record presents one coherent recommended stack and lists alternatives separately with tradeoffs.
Unresolved choices remain visibly provisional/open and are not presented as user-confirmed decisions.
